title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms available to create paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] and is reported as a descriptive summary only. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, explicitly label the one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but introduces safety risks: incorrect sequencing, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys document LLM hallucination and prompt sensitivity that materially affect correctness for code and structured outputs, motivating system architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

We conducted a preregistered paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) to isolate the incremental effect of downstream deterministic validation and a single permitted repair when the exact same sampled initial generation is reused by both arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Our research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate, to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus at most one repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing that candidate unmodified (baseline)?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from a synthetic stress corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and artifacted analysis showing baseline = 995/1000, guarded = 1000/1000, paired difference = 0.005; preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 (primary inferential outcome). (3) Clarification of interpretive consequences of shared_initial_candidate semantics and of a preregistered descriptive bootstrap CI that can exclude zero under extremely sparse discordant counts. (4) Public‑style artifact grounding (preregistration SHA‑256 noted below and in the execution manifest) to support reproducibility and follow‑ups.
sections.related_work:
LLM failures on structured outputs, including hallucinations and strong prompt sensitivity, are documented across multiple evaluations and surveys; these failures motivate validators and constrained output methods for safety‑sensitive domains [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning have been demonstrated to reduce syntactic and executable errors in structured domains; much of that evidence comes from non‑NetOps domains, so transfer depends on validator fidelity and tooling [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI works propose guarded architectures, digital‑twin validation, and protocol‑mediated execution (proof‑carrying traces) as governance mechanisms; these papers present prototypes and benchmarks or conceptual proposals arguing that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and external governance rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Crucially for our design, the literature does not uniformly provide large‑scale production evidence that generate→validate→repair pipelines fully eliminate semantic or long‑tail multi‑step NetOps failures. Some experimental results suggest measurable improvement in controlled scenarios, but improvements depend on model, validator fidelity, and task distribution. Our study is positioned to isolate the downstream verifier/repair contribution under tightly controlled shared_initial_candidate semantics, rather than to evaluate independent prompt/decoding interventions or multi‑model generality.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized before any hosted‑model invocation; its preregistration_sha256 archived in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) was specified as a secondary descriptive summary.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretation. The archived generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate means baseline and guarded episodes begin from the identical sampled candidate; under this design only downstream deterministic validation and the permitted repair call(s) can create paired outcome differences. The design therefore isolates downstream intervention effects and does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed.

Model and runtime configuration. The declared model/provider (execution/model_configuration.json) is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0). The validator implements deterministic digital‑twin checks: required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, group/maintain constraints, and emits a structured validator trace and a binary safe‑deploy verdict per episode.

Task corpus and selection. Tasks were drawn deterministically from the preregistered challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile (selection rule fixed in the preregistration) producing exactly 1000 unique task indices spanning difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). Each task manifest includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and explicit workflow policies used by the validator for deterministic scoring (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation).

Execution protocol, retries, and missingness. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments (primary: 'complete_pair_primary'; sensitivity: failures treated as unsafe). The adapter recorded provider call events and stage counts; repairs were permitted only when the validator rejected the candidate and the adapter invoked the single allowed repair call as specified.

Analysis plan. The preregistered confirmatory test is the exact two‑sided McNemar on the 2×2 paired contingency table. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is a preregistered descriptive summary only. Multiplicity adjustments for secondary hypothesis claims were preregistered (Holm–Bonferroni) but the paper reports only the preregistered primary confirmatory result and descriptive secondary summaries.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑grounded). The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}, and cache_miss_count = 1005. All deterministic consistency checks passed and no cross‑condition cache reuse was observed.

Primary paired outcomes. The preregistered paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Preregistered confirmatory test and descriptive summaries. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]; this interval is reported as a secondary descriptive summary only. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided test was NOT prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001, we label that result explicitly exploratory/post‑hoc and do not use it to alter the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair diagnostics. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5). Representative episode artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑00000*.json) show repairs were invoked for required_sequence or protected_interface violations: the adapter generated a repair prompt, the model produced a repaired candidate, and the validator accepted the repaired candidate on revalidation. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived in the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts. Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5).

Contamination and exclusions. The preregistered contamination checks found no prompt‑leakage flags and no deterministic emulator errors; contamination_summary.csv is empty and missingness_summary.csv records zero failed or unscorable episodes. No post‑hoc exclusions were applied. All seeds and task_index selection rules were fixed pre‑execution per the preregistration.
sections.discussion:
Inferential hierarchy and bootstrap behavior. The preregistered confirmatory test is the exact two‑sided McNemar; because that test returned p = 0.0625, the preregistered H1 is not supported at α = 0.05. The preregistered paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a descriptive summary and can exclude zero in regimes with extremely sparse discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0). Bootstrapping discrete paired outcomes with very few discordant pairs can produce nonzero percentile bounds even when an exact paired test is not significant; this is a sampling‑distribution phenomenon, not a contradiction of the preregistered inferential hierarchy. We therefore treat the exact McNemar as the primary inferential result and the bootstrap interval as a sensitivity/descriptive diagnostic. Any one‑sided tests are reported only as exploratory because they were not prespecified.

Interpretation within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics only downstream validation and the single permitted repair call could create paired differences. The five observed repairs illustrate that a validator with suitable coverage can correct particular ordering/sequence violations. However, the low repair invocation count limits general inference about repair efficacy across broader failure classes. Distinguishing whether low repair counts arise from the generator producing mostly valid candidates, the synthetic corpus having low initial failure prevalence, or validator permissiveness requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, task distributions, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary reflects deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity: the synthetic corpus and single evaluated model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production equipment and other model families. Conclusion validity: near‑unity baseline success yields sparse discordant counts and limited power to detect small absolute improvements using exact paired tests; the preregistered power calculation had assumed a much lower baseline (~0.60) and therefore does not apply to the observed regime.

Operational implications and recommended preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repairs can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups supported by the archive should include: (1) independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding and sampling effects; (2) repair‑budget sweeps (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns by failure class; (3) broader validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) multi‑model evaluations to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should be preregistered with power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary preregistered inferential outcome is the exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) is reported explicitly as exploratory because it was not prespecified. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
